topicName: Mitigating OWASP Top 10 (SQLi, XSS, CSRF, Clickjacking)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Mitigating OWASP Top 10 Vulnerabilities in Django"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Web security is paramount when building robust applications. The OWASP Top 10 represents the most critical security risks to web applications. Fortunately, Django comes with secure defaults and built-in protections against many of these vulnerabilities. In this tutorial, we will explore how Django handles SQL Injection (SQLi), Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF), and Clickjacking, and how to configure them properly."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. SQL Injection (SQLi)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"SQL Injection occurs when untrusted user input is directly concatenated into a database query, allowing attackers to execute malicious SQL statements. Django's Object-Relational Mapper (ORM) mitigates this by default by using parameterized queries under the hood."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"# SECURE: Django ORM automatically parameterizes queries user = User.objects.filter(username=user_input) # INSECURE: Avoid raw SQL queries with string formatting # user = User.objects.raw("SELECT * FROM auth_user WHERE username = '%s'" % user_input)"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"XSS vulnerabilities allow attackers to inject client-side scripts into web pages viewed by other users. Django's template engine automatically escapes specific characters to prevent HTML and script injection."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"

{{ user_comment }}

{{ user_comment|safe }}

"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"CSRF forces an end user to execute unwanted actions on a web application in which they are currently authenticated. Django provides robust CSRF protection via middleware and template tags."},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Ensure that 'django.middleware.csrf.CsrfViewMiddleware' is included in your MIDDLEWARE setting inside settings.py. Then, include the CSRF token in all POST forms."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"
{% csrf_token }}
"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Clickjacking"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Clickjacking is an attack where a site tricks a user into clicking on something different from what the user perceives. Django mitigates this through the X-Frame-Options middleware, which prevents your pages from being loaded inside an iframe."},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Verify that 'django.middleware.clickjacking.XFrameOptionsMiddleware' is active in your MIDDLEWARE settings."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"# settings.py MIDDLEWARE = [ ... 'django.middleware.security.SecurityMiddleware', 'django.contrib.sessions.middleware.SessionMiddleware', 'django.middleware.common.CommonMiddleware', 'django.middleware.csrf.CsrfViewMiddleware', 'django.contrib.auth.middleware.AuthenticationMiddleware', 'django.contrib.messages.middleware.MessageMiddleware', 'django.middleware.clickjacking.XFrameOptionsMiddleware', ] # Sets the default X-Frame-Options header to DENY X_FRAME_OPTIONS = 'DENY'"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always rely on the Django ORM to prevent SQL Injection."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Avoid using the |safe filter on untrusted user data to prevent XSS."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always include {% csrf_token %} in state-changing HTML forms."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Keep XFrameOptionsMiddleware enabled to protect against clickjacking attacks."}]
